clue.text: Ballast, unpopular with dieters ?

definitions.meaning: something added merely to bring a load up to the required mass
read as an instruction to put on pounds, which slimmers avoid

explanation.definitionFit: Filler added to tip a scale is ballast in effect, and gaining pounds is what slimmers dread.

clue.text: Frequently ineffective little schemers

parts.note: recalls Burns: the best-laid schemes of small rodents and men often go awry

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns's poem To a Mouse says the best-laid schemes of mice and men often go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rodents in Burns's poem make plans that come to nothing, like those of men.

clue.text: A grateful, perhaps, if do-nothing ruler

definitions.text: A grateful, perhaps, if do-nothing ruler

parts.words: A grateful, perhaps, if do-nothing ruler
parts.note: grateful is read as grate-full, a hearth filled with timber; Aesop's frogs were given an idle wooden monarch

explanation.walkthrough: 'grateful' means 'a grate full', something filling a fireplace. In Aesop's fable the frogs asking for a king got a lump of timber that did nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's fable the frogs were sent a wooden block as monarch, a byword for a passive ruler.

clue.text: Lucky sprig of a more-than-red-hot momma ?

parts.note: metal heated beyond red heat glows white, so this is white heat
a mother is a woman, referred to as her

explanation.surface: A good-luck spray of flowers belongs to a very sexy mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red-hot momma' looks like a sultry woman; it gives WHITE HEAT (hotter than red heat) and HER. A sprig of white heather is a Scottish good-luck charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of pale-flowered heath is traditionally carried in Scotland as a charm for good fortune.

clue.text: Is a British giant in charge of Introductions?

parts.note: taken as written
Gog is one of the legendary giants of Britain, paired with Magog

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a British giant is running the introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants linked with ancient Britain and the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Isagogic is a formal adjective meaning introductory, used especially of preliminary study of scripture.

clue.text: What the law had to say to Mr Bumble ?

definitions.text: What the law had to say to Mr Bumble

parts.words: What the law had to say to Mr Bumble
parts.note: in Oliver Twist the beadle declares that the law is a ass, so the law would answer in a donkey's voice

explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, Mr Bumble says 'the law is a ass'. If so, the law would speak like a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's bray is the sound an ass makes, fitting Bumble's insult to the law.

clue.text: Far-reaching wish ?

definitions.meaning: to yearn or hanker for something

explanation.definitionFit: A long reach goes far, and to long for something is to yearn for it.

clue.text: "The puff ——, or puff by implication" (Sheridan)

definitions.text: The puff ——, or puff by implication" (Sheridan)

parts.words: The puff ——, or puff by implication" (Sheridan)
parts.note: a quotation from Sheridan's play The Critic, where Mr Puff lists kinds of puff, with one word left blank

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the blank: Mr Puff in Sheridan's The Critic lists the puff direct, preliminary, collateral, collusive, and the puff oblique, or puff by implication.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect or slanting praise works by implication, just as the quotation glosses the missing word.

clue.text: What becomes a chaperone? O, sober grey, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise to make the answer

parts.note: taken as written, the exclamation O, which the OCR misread as a zero

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the drab grey outfit suited to a chaperone.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read the letter O as a zero. 'perhaps' says to rearrange O SOBER GREY. To play gooseberry is British for being an unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To play gooseberry is to be the unwanted third party with a courting couple, as a chaperone is.

clue.text: Postulants cause Mrs Morel a set-back

parts.note: Candida Morell is the title heroine of Shaw's play Candida

indicators.note: the back half of the word set-back tells us to read set in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone causes a setback for a fictional housewife named Mrs Morel.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Morell', Shaw's spelling. 'back' turns SET into TES, which follows CANDIDA. Postulants are people applying for admission, as candidates are.
explanation.definitionFit: Postulants are applicants seeking admission, especially to a religious order, so they are hopefuls standing for selection.

clue.text: One of the Nine about to back oil

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about

indicators.note: to back something here means to send the word oil the other way

explanation.surface: One of nine people is about to put money behind oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OIL into LIO. The Nine are the nine Muses of Greek myth; Clio is the Muse of history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses number nine in classical myth, and Clio presides over history.

clue.text: Rich men contain Scots island anger in the factories

indicators.note: in places the island and the anger within the factories

parts.note: mills are factories
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: Wealthy men keep a lid on Scottish islanders' fury in their factories.
explanation.walkthrough: IONA and IRE go inside MILLS; 'contain' just carries the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Men worth a seven-figure sum are wealthy by definition.

clue.text: Epidemic going East in the pipeline

parts.note: influenza, a widespread outbreak illness, shortened to flu
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An epidemic heading east is already in the pipeline, about to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pipeline' looks like an idiom for 'coming soon', but the definition is just 'pipeline'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct is a pipe carrying smoke and gases away from a fire.

clue.text: It's tricky for a slave-girl to lose a quid!

indicators.note: tricky suggests letters twisted into an awkward new arrangement

explanation.surface: It is hard luck for a servant girl to lose a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' tells us to rearrange LOSE A QUID into the answer. A quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or concubine in an Ottoman harem.

clue.text: For diversions, people with the street up follow 10 for instance

indicators.note: follow says the people and the street come after the muse

parts.note: 10 across is one of the Nine Muses, an example of a muse
men means people in general

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading upwards, so the street abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Pastimes for people as the street goes up after a muse leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ST to TS in this down answer. A MUSE (10, Clio, is one) comes first, then MEN and TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversions are pastimes, entertainments that amuse.

clue.text: There's a snare in the black art drawing

indicators.note: in places the snare inside the black art

parts.note: sorcery, i.e. magic
a net is a trap or snare

explanation.surface: A trap lurks within a sinister piece of black-magic artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like a picture but means pulling towards, as a magnet does. NET goes inside MAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawing iron filings towards it attracts them, like a lodestone.

clue.text: Army record-holder ?

parts.note: Army is read as arm-y, belonging to the arm; record-holder is the cardboard cover for a gramophone disc

explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' suggests soldiers, but read it as 'of the arm': the part of a garment covering the arm, also the cover that holds a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat's arm covering shares its name with the paper jacket in which a vinyl disc is kept.

clue.text: Not much energy for a preliminary exam

parts.note: little means not much
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: A student without much energy faces a first-stage test.
explanation.walkthrough: The Little-go was the old first examination for a Cambridge degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge undergraduates once sat an entrance examination known by this informal name.

clue.text: Touch one's cap to Salvation Army music-maker

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Doffing one's hat to a Salvation Army bandsman.
explanation.walkthrough: SA plus LUTE. To touch one's cap is a respectful greeting, a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a hand to the brim of one's hat is a gesture of respectful greeting.

clue.text: Opera girl would get changed, use talc

indicators.note: would get changed signals a set of letters swapped into a new order

explanation.surface: An opera singer changing costumes reaches for talcum powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would get changed' says to rearrange USE TALC. Manon Lescaut is the heroine of operas by Puccini and Massenet (Massenet's is just Manon).
explanation.definitionFit: Manon Lescaut is the title heroine of Puccini's opera, a young woman of that surname.

clue.text: And is our strange Nessie one such creature?

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters are put into an odd new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the Loch Ness Monster is some sort of prehistoric beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' says to rearrange AND IS OUR. Nessie, the Loch Ness Monster, is often pictured as a surviving plesiosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loch Ness Monster is popularly imagined as a prehistoric reptile that escaped extinction.

clue.text: Reacting to cold, like winter in France?

parts.note: as means like
hiver is French for winter

explanation.surface: Someone responds to the cold the way a French winter would.
explanation.walkthrough: AS plus HIVER, French for winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling and shaking is how the body responds to chilly weather.

clue.text: Poor Alicia's lost a quartz specimen

indicators.note: poor implies the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging
lost tells us the letter a is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: Poor Alicia has lost a piece of quartz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes an A out of ALICIAS, leaving LICIAS, and 'Poor' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide, the mineral compound silica.

clue.text: His work is simply entrancing

parts.note: entrancing sounds like praise for charm, but literally means putting people into a trance, a hypnotist's job

explanation.walkthrough: 'entrancing' reads as 'delightful' but is meant literally: putting people into a trance, as followers of Mesmer did.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist puts subjects into a trance, named after the pioneer Franz Mesmer.

clue.text: Pale ? Have a shot

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A pale person is urged to have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a shy is British for having a try; a coconut shy is a fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen-faced and grey like the residue of a fire describes a wan complexion.

clue.text: Pull upward

indicators.note: in a down answer up means reading from bottom to top, so ward runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written; the run inside upward is a coincidence of the split, not a hidden word, since up is the instruction and ward the piece

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'upward' into 'up' and 'ward': in a down entry WARD read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul or tug something towards you is to drag it.

clue.text: When the main water-supply is well below the mark

definitions.text: When the main water-supply is well below the mark

parts.words: When the main water-supply is well below the mark
parts.note: the main is the sea, not a water pipe, and the mark is the high-tide line, reached least at this kind of tide

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' suggests a water main, but it is the sea (the briny main); a neap tide has the smallest rise, falling well short of the high-water mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is the tide of least range, occurring at the moon's quarters, when high water peaks lowest.

clue.text: Motorist on a collision course with this machine?

definitions.text: Motorist on a collision course with this machine

parts.words: Motorist on a collision course with this machine
parts.note: a motorist who causes a pile-up is a reckless driver; the same name belongs to a machine hammering posts into the ground

explanation.walkthrough: A motorist heading for a pile-up is, as a pun, a pile-driver, the name of a machine that hammers posts into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Construction rigs that ram stakes into the earth share their name with a crash-causing motorist.

clue.text: Declines to be seen at Wimbledon

definitions.meaning: goes down, as the sun does in the evening
Wimbledon is the London tennis championship, where matches are divided into units of games

explanation.definitionFit: The sun goes down in the evening, and tennis matches at Wimbledon, London's grass-court championship, are scored in groups of games.

clue.text: Human wind-indicator?

parts.note: a straw in the wind shows its direction, so a person made of straw is a human weather-vane; the phrase means a sham person

explanation.walkthrough: A straw in the wind shows which way it blows, so a person made of straw is a human weathervane. The phrase means a feeble or sham opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw figure, a feeble sham argument or person, is jokingly treated as a living weather-vane.
